office_categories.label: Lines
office_categories.summary: Straight, bent, and curved relationship contours.

office_categories.label: Basic Shapes
office_categories.summary: Geometric bodies, boundaries, radial contours, and literal symbols.

office_categories.label: Block Arrows
office_categories.summary: Filled directional bodies for sequence, movement, and route emphasis.

office_categories.label: Flowchart
office_categories.summary: Conventional flowchart notation for explicit process diagrams.

office_categories.label: Stars and Banners
office_categories.summary: Emblems, bursts, banners, scrolls, and wave accents.

office_categories.label: Callouts
office_categories.summary: Annotation bodies and leaders that point to another object or region.

office_categories.label: Action Buttons
office_categories.summary: Visual navigation-control shapes whose actions must be assigned separately.

groups.label: Straight lines and connectors
recommended_for: Direct links, dividers, leaders, and reading-path spines.
Thin relationships whose meaning comes from endpoints, routing, or an optional marker.
avoid_for: Do not substitute a line for a filled directional body or content carrier.
Do not imply endpoint attachment; newly authored connector presets remain unconnected.

line.intent: Straight line with the default diagonal orientation.

lineInv.intent: Straight line with the inverse default diagonal orientation.

straightConnector1.intent: Straight connector contour when connector object identity matters.

groups.label: Bent connectors
recommended_for: Orthogonal routing around content or between aligned zones.
Relationships whose route needs visible right-angle structure.
avoid_for: Do not add bends when a straight relationship is clearer.
Do not use the extra segments as decoration or imply unsupported endpoint attachment.

bentConnector5.intent: Four-bend orthogonal connector for more complex routing.

groups.label: Curved connectors
recommended_for: Soft rerouting, feedback links, or relationships that must pass around objects.
Continuous paths where curvature carries meaning.
avoid_for: Do not curve a direct link merely to make it look less plain.
Do not imply unsupported endpoint attachment.

curvedConnector5.intent: Four-segment curved connector for complex routing.

groups.label: Neutral rectangular carriers
recommended_for: Content ownership, stable fields, and nodes that need no directional or symbolic inflection.
Layouts where the absence of contour meaning is itself useful.
avoid_for: Do not choose neutrality only because primitive syntax is shorter.
Do not wrap every text block when spacing already communicates ownership.

rect.intent: Fully neutral rectangular field or carrier.

roundRect.intent: Uniformly rounded carrier with a softer, more approachable boundary.

groups.label: Corner-inflected rectangles
recommended_for: Carriers whose rounded or clipped corners mark an entry edge, open edge, or deck-wide contour language.
Subtle hierarchy without adding arrows or icons.
avoid_for: Do not scatter corner variants randomly; the changed corners must have a page-level reason.
Do not let a decorative corner imply direction that the content does not have.

round1Rect.intent: One rounded corner for a single softened or attached edge.

round2SameRect.intent: Two rounded corners on one side, creating a clear opening or terminal edge.

round2DiagRect.intent: Two diagonally opposed rounded corners for reciprocal or diagonal tension.

snipRoundRect.intent: Mixed clipped and rounded corners for controlled technical contrast.

snip1Rect.intent: One clipped corner for a single technical or directional cue.

snip2SameRect.intent: Two clipped corners on one side for an open or connected edge.

snip2DiagRect.intent: Two diagonally clipped corners for diagonal rhythm or contrast.

groups.label: Triangular bodies
recommended_for: Apex, escalation, directional focus, or a literal triangular object.
Corner anchoring where a diagonal edge materially organizes the page.
avoid_for: Do not use as a generic card; an apex or diagonal edge creates a strong inference.
Do not replace a true arrow when movement or endpoint direction is the job.

triangle.intent: Symmetric triangle for apex, priority, or upward/downward focus.

rtTriangle.intent: Right triangle for corner anchoring, diagonal split, or literal geometry.

groups.label: Slanted quadrilaterals
recommended_for: Motion, transformation, comparison, or a sloped handoff between zones.
Nodes where the slanted sides reinforce the reading direction.
avoid_for: Do not use the diamond as a fake flowchart decision outside an actual flowchart.
Do not use slanted edges on static content with no directional meaning.

diamond.intent: Four-sided focal node for branching, opposition, or a literal diamond.

parallelogram.intent: Parallel slants for motion, transfer, or input/output-like movement.

trapezoid.intent: Symmetric widening or narrowing for expansion, compression, or stage change.

nonIsoscelesTrapezoid.intent: Asymmetric widening or narrowing for off-axis transition.

groups.label: Regular polygon bodies
recommended_for: Compact nodes, numbered stages, badges, or radial systems where side count supports the visual language.
Focal carriers that need more presence than a circle or rectangle.
avoid_for: Do not encode a number merely by matching the polygon side count unless readers benefit.
Do not use many unrelated polygon families on one page.

heptagon.intent: Seven-sided emblematic node with unusual visual rhythm.

decagon.intent: Ten-sided near-circular badge with faceted edges.

dodecagon.intent: Twelve-sided near-circular badge or radial node.

groups.label: Organic carriers
recommended_for: Soft focal zones, ports, lenses, or organic contrast against angular geometry.
Overlap and containment when a continuous curved edge improves grouping.
avoid_for: Do not default to circles for every metric or icon.
Do not use a teardrop unless its pointed end has a focus or direction.

ellipse.intent: Continuous oval field, focal lens, or soft node.

teardrop.intent: Rounded body with one pointed focus for origin, destination, or literal drop imagery.

groups.label: Ornamental carriers
recommended_for: A single high-emphasis label, title plate, or inset whose edge treatment matches the deck language.
avoid_for: Do not repeat as ordinary cards; concave corners or beveling create ceremonial emphasis.
Do not use solely to make a box look less plain.

plaque.intent: Concave-corner plate for a formal label, title, or emblem.

bevel.intent: Beveled rectangular body for a raised or inset focal surface.

groups.label: Radial contours and segments
recommended_for: Cycles, apertures, partial reveals, circular zoning, or a curved page spine.
Non-quantitative radial structure where the contour itself guides reading.
avoid_for: Do not imply a measured proportion unless the angle is backed by data.
Do not imitate a pie or donut chart when a native data chart is required.

pieWedge.intent: Single circular wedge for a radial anchor or literal sector.

pie.intent: Circle with an adjustable missing sector for reveal or incomplete-cycle meaning.

blockArc.intent: Thick curved band for a cycle segment, portal, or curved spine.

donut.intent: Closed ring for circular containment, focus, or a literal ring.

chord.intent: Circular segment bounded by an arc and chord for overlap or partial-reveal geometry.

arc.intent: Open curved contour for a light boundary, trajectory, or partial frame.

groups.label: Frames, corners, and edge pieces
recommended_for: Open ownership boundaries, page apertures, edge anchors, and corner-led composition.
Grouping without turning every content unit into a filled card.
avoid_for: Do not place a frame around content that already has clear ownership.
Do not use folded or diagonal details without a matching page-level edge language.

foldedCorner.intent: Sheet-like carrier or accent with one folded corner.

frame.intent: Closed rectangular frame for a strong aperture or ownership boundary.

halfFrame.intent: Partially open frame for directional grouping or an incomplete boundary.

corner.intent: L-shaped corner piece for edge anchoring or a partial frame.

diagStripe.intent: Diagonal band for edge emphasis, slanted continuity, or a literal stripe.

groups.label: Brackets
recommended_for: Collecting adjacent items, marking a range, or assigning a label to one side of a group.
avoid_for: Do not use when a filled carrier already establishes membership.
Do not mix bracket directions without a clear ownership side.

leftBracket.intent: Left-side bracket that collects content to its right.

rightBracket.intent: Right-side bracket that collects content to its left.

bracketPair.intent: Paired brackets that enclose a complete range or set.

groups.label: Braces
recommended_for: Visible grouping, aggregation, or one-to-many ownership where a bracket is too mechanical.
avoid_for: Do not use as ornamental punctuation detached from a real group.
Do not use paired braces when one-sided assignment is the actual relationship.

leftBrace.intent: Left-side brace that groups or assigns content to its right.

rightBrace.intent: Right-side brace that groups or assigns content to its left.

bracePair.intent: Paired braces that enclose a complete set.

groups.label: Literal pictograms
recommended_for: A concept whose ordinary meaning is exactly the depicted object or symbol.
avoid_for: Do not select by loose metaphor or keyword association.
Do not use as a generic visual-energy substitute for real structure.

cube.intent: Literal cube or compact three-dimensional object.

can.intent: Literal cylinder, database-like store, or container.

lightningBolt.intent: Literal lightning, electricity, shock, or sudden-impact symbol.
avoid_for: Do not use for generic tension, urgency, or price change without literal electrical or shock meaning.

heart.intent: Literal affection, preference, health-heart, or favorite symbol.

sun.intent: Literal sun, daylight, heat, or weather symbol.

moon.intent: Literal moon, night, sleep, or lunar symbol.

noSmoking.intent: Prohibition symbol with an adjustable slash over a target.

cloud.intent: Literal cloud, cloud-computing domain, or atmospheric thought field.

groups.label: Functional pictograms
recommended_for: Literal mechanism, settings, processing, or filtering concepts.
avoid_for: Do not use gears as a generic synonym for every process.
Do not use a funnel unless narrowing, screening, or conversion is the actual relationship.

gear6.intent: Six-tooth gear for a literal mechanism, settings, or interlocking process.

gear9.intent: Nine-tooth gear for a denser literal mechanism or system component.

funnel.intent: Literal filtering, narrowing, qualification, or conversion funnel.

groups.label: Plus symbol
recommended_for: Literal addition, inclusion, medical-cross, or combined-value meaning.
avoid_for: Do not use as a generic decoration between unrelated items.
Use mathPlus when the page is explicitly mathematical notation.

plus.intent: Broad plus or cross body for literal addition, inclusion, or cross symbolism.

groups.label: Corner and edge tabs
recommended_for: Four-corner framing, registration marks, or a technical aperture around a focal zone.
avoid_for: Do not treat the four tabs as independent data points.
Do not add them when a simpler frame already communicates the boundary.

cornerTabs.intent: Four triangular corner tabs defining an implied rectangle.

squareTabs.intent: Four square edge tabs defining an implied rectangle.

plaqueTabs.intent: Four rounded corner tabs defining an implied rectangle.

groups.label: Partition symbols
recommended_for: A literal four- or six-region partition, intersection, or hub motif.
avoid_for: Despite their names, these are not charts and carry no data semantics.
Do not use as a substitute for a native chart or an explained matrix.

chartX.intent: Rectangle divided diagonally into four triangular regions.

chartStar.intent: Rectangle divided into six regions by vertical and diagonal lines.

chartPlus.intent: Rectangle divided into four quarters by vertical and horizontal lines.

groups.label: Arrow-shaped carriers
recommended_for: Stage bodies, handoffs, and compact process steps whose container and direction are one object.
avoid_for: Do not use as a generic card; the pointed end asserts flow.
Do not use when a thin connector between independent nodes is clearer.

homePlate.intent: Pentagon-like horizontal stage body with one pointed destination edge.

chevron.intent: Compact V-notched directional stage for repeated sequence or handoff.

groups.label: Cardinal block arrows
recommended_for: Strong one-way movement, escalation, decline, or a dominant next-step direction.
avoid_for: Do not use for a neutral link or divider.
Do not point toward content unless the endpoint relationship is real.

rightArrow.intent: Strong left-to-right movement or next-step direction.

leftArrow.intent: Strong right-to-left movement, return, or reverse direction.

upArrow.intent: Strong upward movement, growth, or escalation.

downArrow.intent: Strong downward movement, decline, or descent.

groups.label: Stylized forward arrows
recommended_for: Forward motion where the tail treatment communicates acceleration, entry, or interlock.
avoid_for: Do not choose the tail treatment only for novelty.
Do not use when a plain cardinal arrow already expresses the job.

stripedRightArrow.intent: Right arrow with tail stripes for acceleration, launch, or staged entry.

notchedRightArrow.intent: Right arrow with an inward tail notch for interlock or handoff.

groups.label: Multi-axis arrows
recommended_for: Reciprocity, branching, multi-way movement, or a hub with explicit directional alternatives.
avoid_for: Do not imply symmetry or available routes that the content does not support.
Do not use as a generic central decoration.

leftUpArrow.intent: Two-route branch toward left and up.

leftRightUpArrow.intent: Three-route branch toward left, right, and up.

quadArrow.intent: Four-way hub or movement in all cardinal directions.

groups.label: Bent and return arrows
recommended_for: A real turn, reroute, reversal, or return within a process path.
avoid_for: Do not use a turn arrow for generic progress with no change of direction.
Do not confuse a filled turn body with a thin routed connector.

bentArrow.intent: Rounded right-angle route for a directional turn.

uturnArrow.intent: Explicit reversal, return, or loop-back path.

groups.label: Circular arrows
recommended_for: Closed-loop processes, recurrence, refresh, or circular exchange.
avoid_for: Do not imply repetition or reversibility unless it exists.
Do not use as a decorative halo around unrelated content.

circularArrow.intent: One-direction circular loop or refresh path.

leftCircularArrow.intent: Counter-oriented circular loop or return path.

leftRightCircularArrow.intent: Two-way circular exchange or reversible cycle.

groups.label: Curved and swoosh arrows
recommended_for: Directional motion that must arc around a focal object or converge from an offset origin.
avoid_for: Do not add curvature merely to make an arrow more expressive.
Do not use when the path would falsely imply bypass or convergence.

curvedRightArrow.intent: Curved path ending to the right.

curvedLeftArrow.intent: Curved path ending to the left.

swooshArrow.intent: Fast tapered sweep for launch, acceleration, or a dynamic handoff.

groups.label: Arrow callout bodies
recommended_for: A short message whose body and directional emphasis must be one strong object.
avoid_for: Do not use as an ordinary content card.
Do not point in multiple directions unless the message truly applies to each route.

leftArrowCallout.intent: Text-bearing callout with strong leftward direction.

rightArrowCallout.intent: Text-bearing callout with strong rightward direction.

upArrowCallout.intent: Text-bearing callout with strong upward direction.

downArrowCallout.intent: Text-bearing callout with strong downward direction.

leftRightArrowCallout.intent: Text-bearing callout for horizontal two-way emphasis.

upDownArrowCallout.intent: Text-bearing callout for vertical two-way emphasis.

quadArrowCallout.intent: Text-bearing callout for four-way or hub emphasis.

groups.label: Equation operators
recommended_for: An explicit mathematical or logical operator between operands.
avoid_for: Do not use equation symbols as generic separators or decorative icons.
Keep operand order and mathematical meaning unambiguous.

groups.label: Flowchart operations
recommended_for: Exact conventional operation nodes inside an actual flowchart.
avoid_for: Do not use flowchart notation as a decorative card vocabulary.
Do not substitute one operation symbol for another because its contour looks better.

groups.label: Flowchart decisions and routing
recommended_for: Exact branch, merge, junction, or continuation semantics inside an actual flowchart.
avoid_for: Do not infer routing semantics from appearance alone.
Do not use these symbols outside a diagram that explains its flow.

flowChartOffpageConnector.intent: Continuation to another page or diagram frame.

flowChartCollate.intent: Collate or reconcile inputs into an ordered result.

flowChartExtract.intent: Extract one stream or subset from another.

flowChartMerge.intent: Merge multiple flow paths into one.

groups.label: Flowchart input and output
recommended_for: Exact data-entry or presentation nodes inside an actual flowchart.
avoid_for: Do not use obsolete media symbols unless the depicted medium is intentional.
Do not use input/output notation as a general slanted content card.

flowChartPunchedCard.intent: Punched-card input or a deliberately historical medium.

flowChartPunchedTape.intent: Punched-tape input or a deliberately historical medium.

groups.label: Flowchart documents
recommended_for: Document artifacts that enter, leave, or are produced by an actual flowchart.
avoid_for: Do not use the wavy bottom as a generic decorative card edge.

flowChartMultidocument.intent: Multiple document artifacts or a document set.

groups.label: Flowchart storage
recommended_for: Exact storage-media semantics inside an actual flowchart.
avoid_for: Do not choose a storage symbol by silhouette alone.
Use historical media shapes only when that distinction matters.

flowChartMagneticDrum.intent: Magnetic drum or direct-access historical storage.

groups.label: Flowchart terminator
recommended_for: Start, end, or terminal state in an actual flowchart.
avoid_for: Do not use as a generic pill-shaped label when no terminal state is intended.

groups.label: Stars
recommended_for: Literal rating, award, sparkle, burst, or one exceptional focal badge.
avoid_for: Do not use as a routine bullet, card, or unexplained attention device.
High-point stars carry burst or sparkle energy and are poor text carriers.

star5.intent: Conventional rating, award, or favorite star.

star6.intent: Six-point geometric star or literal emblem.

star7.intent: Seven-point unusual emblem or focal burst.

star8.intent: Eight-point badge, compass, or controlled burst.

star10.intent: Ten-point seal-like badge or radial emphasis.

star12.intent: Twelve-point seal-like badge or radial emphasis.

star24.intent: Very dense sparkle or burst accent.

groups.label: Irregular seals and explosions
recommended_for: A literal burst, warning, sale seal, or exceptional interruption.
avoid_for: Do not use for ordinary emphasis or as a recurring section badge.
Do not place long text inside the irregular contour.

irregularSeal1.intent: Irregular burst with a coarser explosion edge.

irregularSeal2.intent: Irregular burst with a denser explosion edge.

groups.label: Straight ribbons
recommended_for: One ceremonial title, milestone, award label, or section banner.
avoid_for: Do not use as a generic content card or repeat on every page.
Do not imply directional arrows from ribbon tails unless the reading path supports it.

ribbon.intent: Banner with the center panel raised above its folded ends.

ribbon2.intent: Banner with the center panel lowered below its folded ends.

leftRightRibbon.intent: Straight ribbon with outward left and right tail emphasis.

groups.label: Curved ribbons
recommended_for: A single arched title or badge whose curvature is part of the page composition.
avoid_for: Do not bend ordinary labels for decoration alone.
Do not use when the curve conflicts with the page's reading axis.

ellipseRibbon.intent: Curved ribbon arcing upward around a central label.

ellipseRibbon2.intent: Curved ribbon arcing downward around a central label.

groups.label: Scrolls
recommended_for: A literal scroll, proclamation, archival document, or deliberately historical motif.
avoid_for: Do not use a scroll as a generic playbook, process card, or long-form content container.
Do not select it merely because the topic mentions a document.

verticalScroll.intent: Tall rolled document or vertical historical proclamation.

horizontalScroll.intent: Wide rolled document or horizontal historical proclamation.

groups.label: Waves
recommended_for: Literal wave, oscillation, fluid motion, or one continuous undulating accent.
avoid_for: Do not use as an arbitrary section divider.
Do not imply volatility or oscillation unless the content supports it.

wave.intent: Single undulating band for literal wave or oscillation.

doubleWave.intent: Double undulating band for stronger ripple or oscillation.

groups.label: Leader-line callouts
recommended_for: A short annotation that must visibly point to one object or region.
Choose bend count and border/accent treatment from the routing and emphasis need.
avoid_for: Do not use as a free-standing content card with no target.
Do not add bends or accent bars that carry no routing or hierarchy purpose.

callout1.intent: Unbordered callout with a straight leader.

callout2.intent: Unbordered callout with one bent leader.

callout3.intent: Unbordered callout with a double-bent leader.

accentCallout1.intent: Straight-leader callout with an accent bar but no full border.

accentCallout2.intent: One-bend callout with an accent bar but no full border.

accentCallout3.intent: Double-bend callout with an accent bar but no full border.

borderCallout1.intent: Bordered callout with a straight leader.

borderCallout2.intent: Bordered callout with one bent leader.

borderCallout3.intent: Bordered callout with a double-bent leader.

accentBorderCallout1.intent: Bordered straight-leader callout with an accent bar.

accentBorderCallout2.intent: Bordered one-bend callout with an accent bar.

accentBorderCallout3.intent: Bordered double-bend callout with an accent bar.

groups.label: Wedge and thought callouts
recommended_for: A speech, thought, or annotation body whose wedge visibly identifies the target.
avoid_for: Do not use without a real target.
Use the cloud variant only for thought, uncertainty, or a literal cloud context.

wedgeRectCallout.intent: Rectangular annotation body with a pointed wedge to the target.

wedgeRoundRectCallout.intent: Rounded rectangular annotation body with a pointed wedge.

wedgeEllipseCallout.intent: Oval speech-like annotation body with a pointed wedge.

cloudCallout.intent: Cloud-shaped thought callout with a dotted tail.

groups.label: Action-button controls
recommended_for: Interactive presentation controls when the matching click or hover action will also be assigned.
avoid_for: The preset supplies visual geometry only; it does not create navigation, media, or hyperlink behavior.
Do not use action-button chrome as a decorative icon set in a noninteractive deck.

actionButtonBlank.intent: Blank action-button body for a custom control label or icon.
